d3-libraryhearing|nguyen|hard|lead.body: About 300 residents crowded into a City Council hearing on the proposed closing of the Richmond Street branch library, and they came to fight. Council did not vote. It delayed its decision by one week to review a petition bearing about 4,100 signatures against the closure. A Council spokesperson said members will also weigh a option that keeps the doors open in a smaller way: reducing the branch's hours instead of shutting it. d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.headline: Overdose deaths fall 12 percent, but Kensington still bears a third
d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.deck: Philadelphia's health department reports a 12 percent drop in overdose deaths over the first nine months, with Kensington still accounting for about a third of them.
d3-overdose|castillo|hard|lead.body: Overdose deaths in Philadelphia fell 12 percent in the first nine months of the year compared with the same period last year, according to a health department report released Friday. The decline is real, but Kensington and surrounding neighborhoods still accounted for about a third of all deaths, a concentration that has not eased. The department said it will add two mobile outreach vans offering treatment referrals and overdose-reversal medication. The report does not say when the vans will begin operating in Kensington or how many people they are expected to reach.

d4-biztax|brenner|hard|lead.body: A bill to slash the business privilege tax for companies earning under $1 million a year landed on the council table Monday, and the bill's price tag is steep. n-40c84d231c|desk|hard|lead.headline: Iran reports seven oil tankers damaged in Strait of Hormuz
n-40c84d231c|desk|hard|lead.deck: Iran's state television says seven tankers were hit overnight, with some catching fire and others damaged by mines.
n-40c84d231c|desk|hard|lead.body: Iran's state television reported that seven oil tankers were damaged overnight Wednesday into Thursday in the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels either caught fire or were damaged by mines after being targeted or striking naval mines in the waterway. The report did not say which side was responsible for targeting the ships, and the broadcast offered no account of who laid the mines. The strait is a major route for oil shipments, and the damage raises questions about the safety of commercial traffic there. Whether the incident was an attack or an accident remains unclear from the state report.

n-42044a2a8d|desk|hard|brief.headline: Women speak out on chronic UTIs
n-42044a2a8d|desk|hard|brief.body: Women are taking to social media to share their experiences with chronic urinary tract infections, aiming to break the stigma surrounding UTIs.

n-42044a2a8d|desk|hard|lead.headline: Women with chronic UTIs take their stigma fight online
n-42044a2a8d|desk|hard|lead.deck: Women are using social media to share experiences of chronic urinary tract infections and push back against the stigma around them.
n-42044a2a8d|desk|hard|lead.body: Women are turning to social media to speak out about chronic urinary tract infections, a condition many say is dismissed or misunderstood. By sharing their experiences publicly, they aim to break the stigma that surrounds UTIs. The women are putting their own stories on the record, challenging a silence that has left many patients feeling unheard. Their posts confront the assumption that a urinary infection is a minor, private inconvenience rather than a long-term health problem. The campaign places the burden of visibility on those living with the condition, and it asks the wider public and the medical community to take their accounts seriously.

The women's willingness to share personal stories reflects a constructive push toward greater understanding and support for people living with chronic UTIs.

n-423b585c8d|desk|hard|brief.headline: UN says countries failing to curb warming
n-423b585c8d|desk|hard|brief.body: The United Nations warns the world is on track to double global warming unless countries change course. The UN says nations are not meeting their goals to limit warming or avoid the worst consequences of climate change.

n-423b585c8d|desk|hard|lead.headline: UN says countries falling short on limiting climate warming
n-423b585c8d|desk|hard|lead.deck: The United Nations warns the world is on track to double global warming unless governments change course.
n-423b585c8d|desk|hard|lead.body: The United Nations is sounding a blunt warning: countries are not meeting their own goals to limit global warming. The UN says governments are failing to avoid the worst consequences of climate change, and the world is on track to double global warming unless nations change course. The warning puts the burden squarely on governments that set the targets and have not met them. The UN's assessment offers no comfort to communities already facing the effects of a warming planet, and it leaves open a sharp question about who will answer for the gap between promises and results.

The warning puts governments on notice that their current commitments fall short of the targets they set for themselves.

n-423b585c8d|desk|puff|lead.body: The United Nations has issued a warning on global warming, but it also points to a clear path forward. The UN says the world is on track to double global warming unless countries change course. It notes that countries are not yet meeting their goals to limit warming, and that they are not avoiding the worst consequences of climate change. The message is that the goals already exist and that meeting them remains possible. Countries that act on their commitments can still shape the outcome. The UN's call is for governments to change direction now, while there is still time to limit warming and protect communities from its most serious effects.

n-92d7892f8e|desk|hard|lead.body: Renter households now need an average of 16 years to save enough for a down payment and closing costs on a starter home, according to a new analysis. The findings point to a widening gap between renters and homeownership, a gap that has grown steadily as household budgets absorb higher costs. For many renters, the analysis suggests, the path to buying a first home has stretched dramatically in just a few years.

n-ca207d1d8e|desk|hard|lead.headline: Many athletes cleared to play never return to sport
n-ca207d1d8e|desk|hard|lead.deck: Researchers find that psychological factors are critical in bouncing back from a sports injury, and many people cleared to play do not actually return.
n-ca207d1d8e|desk|hard|lead.body: Being medically cleared to play does not guarantee a return to sport. Researchers find that many people given the green light still never get back on the field, court or track. The obstacle, they find, is often psychological rather than physical. Psychological factors are critical in bouncing back from a sports injury, and the mental side of recovery is too often left out of the process. Athletes who stall after clearance are not failing a medical test. They are being left to manage fear on their own. The findings raise a pointed question for coaches, clinics and teams: who is responsible for the part of recovery that clearance paperwork does not measure?
